task.title: Unhealthy diets among young people
task.scenario: Health services report that many teenagers eat mainly processed food and drink sugary drinks every day.
task.prompt: Many teenagers now eat mostly processed food and drink sugary drinks every day. What problems does this cause for young people and for society? What can be done to improve the situation?
instructions: Make sure you cover all of the points listed.
You are writing for: a general readership. Style: formal.

required_elements: Address: identify at least two problems
Address: explain how they affect society

expected_response.cognitive_demand: Analyse causes, effects and solutions; Plan, advise, suggest

criteria.name: Task fulfilment
criteria.description: How fully and appropriately the response does what the task asks: required points, purpose, audience and, where relevant, position.
criteria.successful_performance: Addresses all parts of the task in a developed way; position or purpose is clear throughout; ideas are relevant and extended with examples. Required points: identify at least two problems; explain how they affect society; propose realistic solutions; say who should act
criteria.weak_performance: A part of the task is ignored or only briefly treated; position unclear or inconsistent; ideas general and unsupported.
criteria.expected_evidence: Which required points are present; how each is supported; whether purpose, audience and position are clear. Check each required point: identify at least two problems; explain how they affect society; propose realistic solutions; say who should act.
criteria.evaluation_limitations: Content knowledge is not assessed; do not penalise factual inaccuracy unless the task asks for accuracy to a supplied source.

criteria.name: Coherence and cohesion
criteria.description: How logically the ideas connect and how clearly linking devices and reference express those connections.
criteria.successful_performance: Information arranged logically; a range of cohesive devices used appropriately; clear progression within paragraphs.
criteria.weak_performance: Mechanical or overused linkers; unclear reference; weak paragraph logic.
criteria.expected_evidence: Order of ideas; variety and accuracy of linkers; clarity of pronoun reference; paragraph logic.
common_error_patterns: misuse of however / on the other hand
criteria.evaluation_limitations: A text can be cohesive and still weak on content; keep this criterion separate from task fulfilment.

criteria.name: Lexical resource
criteria.description: Range, precision and appropriateness of vocabulary, including collocation and word formation.
criteria.successful_performance: Good range with some precision; uses collocation and word formation; errors are occasional and do not obscure meaning.
criteria.weak_performance: Limited precision; repeated phrases; noticeable collocation or word-form errors.
criteria.expected_evidence: Range of topic words; repetition; collocation; word formation; spelling. Expected vocabulary demands: health and diet; public policy; solutions and responsibility.
criteria.evaluation_limitations: Do not reward unusual words that are used incorrectly; do not penalise a plain word that is correct and appropriate.

patterns: relative clause pronoun repetition ('the man who he ...')

l1_transfer_hypotheses.caution: These are hypotheses about common patterns; they are NOT to be reported as a learner weakness from a single instance.

criteria.name: Grammatical range and accuracy
criteria.description: Range of structures used and the accuracy with which they are controlled, including punctuation that affects clarity.
criteria.successful_performance: Variety of complex structures; most sentences error-free; errors persist in less common structures.
criteria.weak_performance: Errors in complex structures reduce clarity at times; reliance on a few patterns.
criteria.expected_evidence: Types of structures; proportion of error-free sentences; kinds of errors; whether errors are systematic. Structures invited by the task: cause_and_effect, modals_obligation_advice, conditionals_unreal, passive_voice.
criteria.evaluation_limitations: Judge by the structures the learner chooses and controls; do not penalise absence of structures the task does not invite.

criteria.name: Organisation and development of ideas
criteria.description: Overall structure of the text and how far main ideas are developed, supported and linked to a position or purpose.
criteria.successful_performance: Clear overall structure with a position, developed paragraphs and a conclusion; main points are explained and exemplified.
criteria.weak_performance: Main ideas not developed; no clear position; repetition.
criteria.expected_evidence: Presence of position/thesis; paragraph topics; reasons and examples per point; conclusion.
common_error_patterns: one-sided treatment of a two-sided task
criteria.evaluation_limitations: Do not apply to very short A1/A2 texts; the task does not require essay structure there.

policy.observed_error_vs_weakness: A diagnostic category is an OBSERVED error pattern when at least one instance is found in a response. It may be reported as an INFERRED learning weakness only after >= 3 instances in one response set of >= 100 words (or >= 2 responses) and when the error is not explained by task demands (for example a tense the task did not invite).

diagnostics.observed_vs_inferred: An error is OBSERVED when an instance appears in the response. It may be recorded as an INFERRED weakness only under the policy in diagnostics.policy (repeated instances, enough text, and not explained by task demands).
